hook.description: Cold open on a stop-motion couple (felt-textured, big-nosed characters) already seated on the couch mid-conversation, TV remote in his hand, her phone in hers. He blurts the confession "I just liked your ex's photo by accident," and she snaps back with a stunned "What?". A small 'Episode 24' watermark and the episode title card 'LIKED EX'S PHOTO' are overlaid on this same opening shot, branding the premise instantly.
hook.why_it_works: No establishing shot or wind-up: the very first line is the embarrassing confession itself, so the premise, stakes, and comedic hook land within 2.5 seconds. The immediate 'What?' gives the viewer a proxy reaction that confirms this is worth watching.

setup.description: He tries to walk the confession back, admitting "I unliked it immediately, but I think she got a notification." The attempted damage-control reveals the fix didn't work, digging the hole deeper while his partner's shocked, wide-eyed expression holds on him (captions render the line word-by-word, e.g. 'GOT' visible on screen).

conflict.description: After a short pause, the partner fires back with a pointed, disbelieving follow-up: "So you're saying you accidentally scrolled seven years?" Her tone and phrasing directly challenge the plausibility of his 'accident' excuse, functioning as the confrontation beat.

punchline.description: The same line that voices the confrontation is also the joke's payoff: the specificity of 'scrolled seven years' exposes that liking an ex's old photo could never be a genuine accident, undercutting his excuse and delivering the comedic twist in a single deadpan question.

ending.description: The scene holds briefly on the couple's frozen, awkward stare after her line lands (a beat of silence, per the pause data, roughly 9.4s-10.1s) before hard-cutting to a black end card with the show's branding.
ending.cta_or_text_overlay: Black card reading 'LOW BATTERY PEOPLE' (title) / 'CREATED BY NIN.' (creator credit) / a yellow ticket-style banner reading 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' — series branding/CTA rather than a resolution to the joke.

beat_map.description: Man confesses to liking his partner's ex's photo by accident; she reacts with 'What?'. Episode title/number overlay stamps the premise on the same shot.
He explains he unliked it immediately but suspects a notification already went out, showing his cover-up attempt failed.

Fused conflict/punchline beat: partner's sarcastic question 'So you're saying you accidentally scrolled seven years?' both confronts his excuse and delivers the comedic twist that exposes it as implausible.
Silent held reaction shot on the couple, then cut to black end card with series title, creator credit, and 'New Episode Daily' banner.

narrative_notes: At only ~12s of live scene time (plus a ~2s black end card), this reel compresses the arc to three dialogue lines: conflict and punchline are genuinely fused into the single closing question ('So you're saying you accidentally scrolled seven years?'), which simultaneously confronts the excuse and delivers the joke's twist -- there is no separate confrontation line before the payoff, so those two schema fields intentionally share identical timestamps and description logic. The hook is unusually front-loaded: the confession itself (rather than any scene-setting) is the very first line of dialogue, with on-screen episode branding ('Episode 24', title card) doubling down on the hook in the same shot rather than delaying it. The ending is a pure branding/CTA card with no diegetic resolution -- the joke's tension (is the excuse believed?) is left unresolved, which is consistent with a recurring-couple sketch format ('Low Battery People') that relies on daily episodic release rather than closure within a single reel.
